name: Motors, pumps, compressors and industrial machines
note: For electric motors, pumps, compressors and related fluid-handling equipment, CBP usually finds that origin is conferred by the manufacture of the core functional mechanism, such as the stator and rotor, impeller, rotary group, compressor unit or heavy-duty machined fluid-end housing, or by extensive local sheet-metal fabrication combined with multi-stage subassembly. Simple mechanical assembly of pre-manufactured motors, impellers, switches, valves and control boards into a housing, or minor finishing of imported blanks, does not. For industrial machines (version 2) the rulings turn on the facts: a robot arm and a metal detector head decided origin over the frames, tooling and assembly added elsewhere, while building an injection moulding machine from about ten subassemblies, with its software programmed there, and assembling a wind turbine nacelle's generator and frames made the assembly country the origin. Written from 10 CBP substantial-transformation rulings outside the dev and held-out splits (D212), with four machine rulings from the train pool added in version 2 (D782). Costs are illustrative defaults; users edit them.

groups.name: Motor stator and rotor
operations: Manufacture the motor stator and rotor from laminations and windings
Assemble the motor with capacitors, fan, shaft, mounting plate, and seals

precedent.note: CBP found that manufacturing the stator and rotor in the assembly country conferred origin to a vacuum pump (N344081).

groups.name: Impeller and rotary mechanism
operations: Produce the impeller, cylinder block with piston bores, hydraulic pistons, and crankshaft
Cut, spline, and turn the power transmitting driveshaft
Drill balance holes, trim the outside diameter, and bore the inside diameter of the impeller
Construct compressor, evaporator, and condenser cooling subassemblies

precedent.note: CBP held that the origin of a pump is determined by the country where the impeller is produced (N333514), while minor machining of an imported impeller and shaft was not enough to confer origin (N333514).

groups.name: Housing, chassis and machined block
operations: Machine, drill cylinders, heat treat, mill, and bore forged steel blocks into a finished fluid-end housing
Stamp, bend, weld, and powder coat steel sheet into chassis panels and mounting plates
Stretch, form, trim, flange, and punch steel coil into compressor outer shell cases
Cast or mold outer housings, bottom plates, shroud covers, and tanks

precedent.note: Stamping, welding, and powder coating steel chassis panels alongside subassembly production conferred origin (N347270, N347271, N347272), whereas supplying the outer housing and base plate of a vacuum pump did not control origin (N344081).

groups.name: Control boards, switches and valves
operations: Manufacture the printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) and main control board
Assemble float switches, micro-switches, thermostats, sensors, and brackets
Press valve inserts into valve bodies and assemble discharge flanges, tees, and O-rings

precedent.note: Sourcing the PCBA or control board from China (N344081, N347271) or assembling switches, floats, and valves from imported parts (N347899, N351810) was not enough to confer origin over the country producing the core mechanical or structural assemblies. EU-made electronics did not make the EU the origin of an injection moulding machine assembled in Mexico (N349312). No pool ruling rests on where software is loaded alone: in N349312 programming the machine's software in Mexico was one of many Mexican steps.

groups.name: Machine working unit
operations: build the unit that does the machine's work: a robot arm, a metal detection head, a plasticizing and injection unit, or a generator rotor and stator

precedent.note: The unit that does the work decided origin when the rest was frames, tooling and assembly: a Japanese robot arm (N346867) and a Chinese metal detector head (N340920). Assembling the rotor and stator into a nacelle's drivetrain in France was among the processes that made France the origin (N333849). It did not decide for an injection moulding machine: EU-made plasticizing components and servo motors did not outweigh the assembly of about ten subassemblies in Mexico (N349312).

groups.name: Frames, conveyors and tooling
operations: fabricate pedestals, base frames, conveyors and reject units
make end-of-arm tooling, grippers, brackets and fixation blocks
cast or weld machine frames, hubs and large structural parts

precedent.note: Frames and tooling did not decide: a Chinese gripper and pedestal on a Japanese robot arm (N346867), a Mexican conveyor and reject unit around a Chinese detector (N340920), a Chinese nacelle central frame and hub finished in France (N333849) and Chinese cast components in a Mexican injection moulding machine (N349312).

groups.name: Final assembly and testing
operations: Install the motor, impeller, rotary group, or valves into the main housing or chassis
Mount the PCBA, switches, sensors, and covers using fasteners, spacers, and seals
Apply grease or lubricating oil, seal the unit, and perform final testing
Program and configure the machine's control software, then run mechanical and electrical tests

precedent.note: Final assembly conferred origin when combined with local steel chassis fabrication and key subassembly manufacturing (N347270, N347271, N347272), or when a machine was built from about ten subassemblies with its software programmed there (N349312) or a nacelle's generator and frames were assembled and joined there (N333849); simply assembling imported components like impellers, motors and housings was not enough (N333514, N347899, N351810), nor mounting a finished robot arm on a pedestal with a gripper and camera (N346867) or joining a detector head to a conveyor and reject unit (N340920).
